Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the run-chase to begin! The two Umpires make their way out to the middle and so do the fielders of Sri Lanka who spread out in the field. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran are the two openers for Afghanistan. Angelo Mathews has the new ball and is all in readiness to bowl the first over of the chase. Let's play...
...The Run Chase...

Right then, Sri Lanka has posted a decent total on the board and the tourists will have to be at their A-game to chase it down. A riveting second half of the match is up on the cards. Stay tuned, folks as the chase begins shortly.

Afghanistan began fabulously as Fazalhaq Farooqi removed Nissanka in the first over and Kusal Mendis in his second. Naveen Ul Haq too, dismissed the good-looking de Silva inside the Powerplay. Noor Ahmed was brought into the attack and he too, picked a wicket in his very first over. The ball was moving a bit but not too much which helped their bowlers to exploit the conditions well, but more than that, their execution was spot on. But sooner, they lost the track and were all over the place when Hasaranga took them to the cleaners. But after the crucial wicket of Hasaranga by Naveen, they crept back into the contest as their bowlers put brakes on the runs and conceded just 21 runs in the last four overs in the slog phase and bowled Sri Lanka out in the penultimate over itself. Fazalhaq Farooqi finished with a brilliant 3-fer and was complimented well in the end by Azmat and Naveen who picked two apiece and restricted them on 160.

Phew, what an eventful and dynamic first half of play we've witnessed here at Dambulla. The conclusion wasn't quite what Sri Lanka had hoped for, especially after Hasaranga's aggressive onslaught during the middle overs. Sri Lanka encountered an early setback with the departure of the in-form Pathum Nissanka in the opening over. Subsequently, Kusal Mendis struggled to find his rhythm at the crease. Despite Dhanajaya de Silva's attempt to inject aggression with quick boundaries, his inning was short-lived, ending on 24. Charith Asalanka's departure with a single-digit score added to Sri Lanka's woes. However, the tide turned with skipper Wanindu Hasaranga's aggressive onslaught, breathing life back into the team. Hasaranga's explosive start, coupled with Sadeera Samarawickrama's steady support, revived Sri Lanka's innings. Hasaranga's rapid half-century off just 24 deliveries bolstered their recovery, though Samarawickrama's run-out halted their momentum. Nevertheless, Hasaranga's well-crafted 67 runs in the 16th over steered Sri Lanka away from the early collapse, as they amassed 55 runs in the middle overs. Despite their resurgence, Sri Lanka faced a slowdown in the run rate after Hasaranga's dismissal, resulting in quiet overs and a premature end to their innings, falling short of the allotted 20 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-match formalities and it's now time to let the action begin at Dambulla. The two Umpires are out in the middle and the fielders of Afghanistan stroll out before spreading to their respective field positions. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis are the two openers for Sri Lanka and it will be Fazalhaq Farooqi to bowl the first over of the first T20I for Afghanistan. Let's play...
The teams have lined up for their respective national anthems. It will be Afghanistan's anthem first and Sri Lanka's anthem will follow next.

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawayo is down for the pitch report and says it is 24 degrees and there is a lovely flow of breeze across the stadium. He adds that there is a nice grass cover which is thin and dry and might not help the seamers a lot and the few cracks might cause the ball to misbehave a bit later on. He concludes that it looks like a nice batting deck and the bowlers will have to bowl well later on.

Wanindu Hasaranga says they would have bowled first too but they have a well-balanced team and it won't matter a lot. He adds that they have played 3 good games and will look to do the same. He concludes that Binura Fernando and Matheesha Pathirana come into the squad.

Ibrahim Zadran, the skipper of Afghanistan won the toss and chose to BOWL first. He says that they have little idea about the wicket so it's safe to bowl first. Says no new guys in the team, the boys have been playing different leagues but now they are back.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran (C), Gulbadin Naib, Azmatullah Omarzai, Najibullah Zadran, Mohammad Nabi, Karim Janat, Qais Ahmad, Noor Ahmad, Fazalhaq Farooqi, Naveen-ul-Haq.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Dhananjaya de Silva, Sadeera Samarawickrama, Charith Asalanka, Angelo Mathews, Dasun Shanaka, Wanindu Hasaranga (C), Maheesh Theekshana, Binura Fernando, Matheesha Pathirana.
TOSS UPDATE: Afghanistan won the coin flip and elected to BOWL first.

Afghanistan on the other hand put up a valiant fight in the second Test match and also on a couple of occasions in the ODIs but the T20 format is their strongest suit and they will be looking to get a win of two against their Asian counterparts. Their talisman, Rashid Khan is still a big miss but they have some great individuals who can turn the game on its head. Let's see which side takes the early lead in the series. Toss and team news in a bit.

The hosts Sri Lanka had a good outing in the only-Test but they absolutely dominated with the bat in the three-match ODI series with Pathum Nissanka scoring a couple of tons including a double century. Wanindu Hasaranga will be hoping to lead his side to a series win and get the preparations underway for the T20 World Cup in a few months time.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 1st T20I between Sri Lanka and Afghanistan in Dambulla. This is the final leg of Afghanistan's tour to Sri Lanka and the visitors will be looking to end the tour on a high whereas the hosts will look to make it three series wins out of three.
... MATCH DAY ...

After Sri Lanka's comprehensive clean sweep in the ODI series, the attention now shifts to the T20I series, the most consequential leg of Afghanistan's tour of the island nation with the T20 World Cup on the horizon. Sri Lanka will eye to replicate their success in the ODI series, whereas Afghanistan will take to the field to avenge the whitewash inflicted on them. Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium in Dambulla will play host to all three games of the T20I series. The change in format has brought a change in leadership for the Lankans, with Wanindu Hasaranga assuming the charge. Pathum Nissanka will aim to translate his ODI form into the shorter format of the game. Other than him, the onus will be on Kusal Mendis, Kusal Perera, and Charith Asalanka. The all-rounder contingent consists of skipper Wanindu Hasaranga, Angelo Mathews, and Dasun Shanaka as the experienced names. As he does in both white-ball formats, Maheesh Theekshana will lead the spin department, with Akila Dananjaya and Kamindu Mendis as the other specialist spin options. Dilshan Madushanka will spearhead the pace attack, and he will have Binura Fernando, Nuwan Thushara, and Matheesha Pathirana for company. As far as Afghanistan are concerned, Ibrahim Zadran will continue to be the captain of their ship, and he will be hoping to lead the way with the bat, something he could not do in the previous T20I series against India. The move to promote Gulbadin Naib to the top order has done wonders for them, and he is likely to retain his batting spot at number 3. Rahmanullah Gurbaz stands out in the batting unit, and his performances will be decisive in the outcome of the series. As witnessed in the ODI series, Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi pack a punch with both bat and ball and continue to do so in this format as well. The absence of Mujeeb Ur Rahman is a big blow for the Afghans, and Noor Ahmad and Qais Ahmad will be expected to fill that void. On the pace bowling front, Fazalhaq Farooqi and Naveen-ul-Haq are the usual suspects and will play a key role up front as well as at the death. Unlike the ODI series, the T20I series promises to be highly competitive and we are in for three mouthwatering games. Who are you backing to take the lead in the series?
